newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota winter wheat seeding behind normal.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota winter wheat seeding behind normal.

text.p: Winter wheat seeding continued well behind normal but got into full swing during the week ended September 15, the weekly state crop report said.

Winter wheat seeding increased 19 points from last to 27 percent seeded but this well behind the normal pace of 43 percent. Producers are hoping the winter wheat will get a few inches of growth before the first freeze.
Row crops made good progress but an early freeze within the next couple of weeks could severely affect the yields of late-planted crops.

The amount of corn reaching the dough stage rose to 96 percent, slightly behind last year but four points ahead of the five-year average. Fourteen percent was mature, well behind the normal of 30 percent, but some high-moisture corn was harvested.
The amount of soybeans dropping leaves increased 21 points to 56 percent, ahead of the five-year average of 44 percent.
The amount mature, at 22 percent, was also ahead of the normal of 19 percent. Some soybeans in the north central part of the state were beginning to be harvested.
